newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says he won't talk money with Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says he won't talk money with Chirac.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday he would not discuss the value of the lira with France as President Jacques Chirac arrived to meet him after a prickly exchange over monetary union.

The leaders shook hands on a red carpet at Naples' Capodichino airport to the strains of a military brass band, putting behind them all signs of anger that flared after Chirac said Italy may not be ready at the single currency's launch.

Chirac's comments earlier in the week had almost led Italy to scrap their summit. A similar meeting with Prodi's predecessor Lamberto Dini was planned for last year but was called off by Chirac during a row over French nuclear testing.
Chirac swiftly backpedalled, saying he "ardently hoped" Italy would be ready for the planned launch date of January 1, 1999, and praising Prodi's tought "budget for Europe".

His spokeswoman Catherine Colonna said on Wednesday that France hoped that Italy could soon rejoin Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) which it crashed out of spectacularly amid currency turmoil in September 1992.
But she said France wanted to see the lira strengthen first.
Prodi told reporters shortly after arriving in this southern port city that talks on the right level for the lira to re-enter the ERM would not be on the agenda of the two-day meeting.
"It is not a dialogue that can be done at a bilateral level," he said. "The question of reentry will be discussed at a collective level (with all European Union partners)."
With bilateral meetings and a EU summit in Dublin at the weekend, Prodi said he hoped that could get under way soon.
"It's clear that talks on the re-entry into the so-called snake cannot be delayed for long," he said.

Prodi's centre-left government on Thursday presented its 1997 deficit-busting budget to parliament but the plans to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's debt, with the help of a "Euro-tax", were met with stiff opposition.
Prodi insists that the stringent measures would ensure that Italy would be a founder member of the European single currency, to be called the "euro".

"If you don't prepare now, you won't pass the exam in 1998," said Prodi, a former economics professor. EU states are due to decide in spring 1998 who will qualify for monetary union, based on economic data from next year.

Chirac clapped Prodi on the back warmly on arrival for what one economist has dubbed the "kiss-and-make-up summit". The two leaders then went on to a formal dinner hosted by Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro.
Their main talks, face-to-face and then with financial, foreign and other ministers present, will take place on Friday morning at the city's Bourbon Royal Palace.

The Naples meeting is being watched with great interest by investors who have recently poured into the Italian lira and bonds. Some feel Chirac will make amends for his gaffe by giving another vote of confidence to Italian monetary union hopes.

Chirac has complained that a weak lira hurts French competitiveness but the exchange rate sums are taxing for Prodi because Italy's economy, and export industries, stand to lose out if the lira rejoins the ERM at too high a level.

He has been quoted recently as saying that around 1,050 to the German mark would be appropriate for re-entry, but on Thursday the currency was at around its highest level since August 1994 at 990 to the German mark.
